summary: Frontend E2E testing of the NEW 7-day Weekly Plan (PianoUnico) in MikiLab Pro. All 5 required flows PASS: (1) gate PIN + admin login + open 'Weekly Plan' panel (piano-unico) shows piano-saved-badge '24 batches' and the 7 day tabs lun/mar/mer/gio/ven/sab/dom with counts (4/4/4/4/4/4/0) + full day detail (calendar, backward times, timeline, warnings). (2) Persistence after browser reload OK (weeklyApi.get restores days+option_label 'Massima velocità'). (3) Day edits work: modified qty (50->77), start (04:00->06:15), added a manual batch via piano-day-add-lun, deleted a middle batch via piano-batch-del-lun-1, clicked piano-save -> toast 'Weekly plan saved.' and after reload edits were preserved (qty=77, start=06:15). (4) Full LLM generation flow WORKS: filled 2 recipes (Anima Integrale + Baguette a Lievito Madre), clicked piano-generate -> 3 options (Massima velocità / Massima qualità / Risparmio personale) appeared in ~25s with per-day chips; clicked piano-option-0 -> piano-detail-loading shown -> full 7-day detail rendered in ~10s with 27 detailed batches, HH:MM starts, backward times header (03:30 wake), Sitor warnings and timeline. (5) No non-noise console errors (only expected pre-gate 401s and harmless THREE.js WebGPU adapter warnings). Rest of Direzione console reachable (Recipes/Plan/Orders/Team/Tools/Sitor/Security nav intact).

issues: Active day defaults to today's weekday (dom in this test) which after reload can show 'No batches for this day' when Sunday has 0 batches — user may think plan is empty; consider defaulting to first day with batches or highlight non-empty tabs.

critical_code_review_comments: PianoUnico.jsx is 496 lines with 3 logical steps + DayPlan sub-component; could be split (DayPlan.jsx, useWeeklyPlan hook) for maintainability but not blocking.
activeDay initialized once with getDay(); when the user has NO batches on today's tab there's no auto-fallback to a populated day (minor UX).

saveAll persists items[] where recipe_id is derived by slugifying product name (line 287) — this loses the original recipe_id when the batch originated from Sitor detail; if downstream analytics rely on recipe_id, they will miss stable joins.

In autoplanWeekDetail path (choose()) the previously-saved 'week' state is wiped (setWeek(null)) BEFORE the LLM call; if the LLM call fails the user loses the on-screen plan and must reload from archive — consider keeping previous week until new detail returns.
seed_data_creation: During tests: edited saved plan Monday batch 0 qty 50->77, start 04:00->06:15; added and then deleted intermediate lots (net 0). A fresh weekly plan for option 'Massima velocità' with 27 detailed batches was regenerated in-memory but NOT saved (piano-save not clicked at end of gen flow), so the archived plan still shows 24 batches with the persisted edits.
context_for_next_testing_agent: PianoUnico now handles the whole 7-day flow (step1 orders -> step2 3 strategies -> step3 7 tabs). Data-testid map: piano-unico, piano-saved-badge, piano-day-tabs, piano-day-tab-<lun|mar|mer|gio|ven|sab|dom>, piano-cal-row-<day>-<i>, piano-batch-{start,product,qty,del}-<day>-<i>, piano-day-add-<day>, piano-recipe-<i>, piano-qty-<i>, piano-add-row, piano-del-row-<i>, piano-extra-orders, piano-generate, piano-option-<0-2>, piano-detail-loading, piano-generated, piano-save, piano-speak, piano-print, piano-calendar, piano-backward, piano-timeline, piano-warnings. LLM Phase-1 latency ~20-25s; Phase-2 detail ~10s (fast because parallel).
